# --fmt formats a named file, outside any project, keeping its comments,
# and a formatted file stays as it is.
bit --fmt example.bit
! stdout .
cmp example.bit formatted.bit.want
bit --fmt example.bit
! stdout .
cmp example.bit formatted.bit.want

# Invalid input is reported and left as it was.
cp invalid.bit.orig broken.bit
! bit --fmt broken.bit
stderr 'broken\.bit'
cmp broken.bit invalid.bit.orig

! bit --fmt example.bit another.bit
stderr 'accepts zero or one \.bit file'

-- example.bit --
# Header

# Command
job=exec{
command='echo # hello' # inline
}
-- formatted.bit.want --
# Header

# Command
job = exec {
  command = 'echo # hello'  # inline
}
-- invalid.bit.orig --
job = exec {
